items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-10-21
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] This is Norman Grant's, they're talking about.

ctx.x: Uh, jazz band. They didn't, they didn't worry about it. Let him pick these own tunes. You know. The only thing the man would give you the sign of the go, and he would tell you if you, a lot of fellas don't start together. Start together, and end together. You know, going out there. Outside of that, you wouldn't worry. He let you make your own balance.
This is Norman Grant's, they're talking about. Uh huh.

And then the records come out much better. Of course, whoever you're recording for, you pick the tunes, you see. You know what tunes you want. But, uh, if you keep, if you're playing the recording, I, I, my mind, the fact is, if you play the tune three times, take one, take two, sometimes you take five and six, you lose it. Yeah. Because, a man is losing interest in that tune. Oh, you're exhausting yourself. Yeah, yeah, you get no interest in it. So, if you take two or three, and you don't get it right. Forget…
